items.title: Blind SSRF via git ls-remote in Gitspace lookup-repo endpoint
items.body:
### Summary

The `POST /api/v1/gitspaces/lookup-repo` endpoint accepts a user-supplied `url` field and passes it directly to `git ls-remote` without validating whether the URL targets a private or internal IP address. Any authenticated user with `InfraProviderView` permission (a low-privilege role) can use this to make the Harness server issue outbound TCP/HTTP connections to arbitrary hosts including internal network addresses and cloud metadata endpoints (e.g., `169.254.169.254`), enabling blind SSRF and internal port scanning.

### Details

**Vulnerable path:**

`app/api/handler/gitspace/lookup_repo.go` -> `HandleLookupRepo` ->
`app/api/controller/gitspace/lookup_repo.go` -> `Controller.LookupRepo` ->
`app/gitspace/scm/scm.go` -> `SCM.CheckValidCodeRepo` -> `detectBranch(ctx, url)` ->
`detectDefaultGitBranch(ctx, url)` ->
`git ls-remote --symref -q <attacker-url> HEAD`

The `sanitizeLookupRepoInput` function at `app/api/controller/gitspace/lookup_repo.go` (lines 78-93) only validates that the URL parses successfully and has a non-empty scheme. It does not check whether the resolved host is a loopback, link-local, or private RFC-1918 address:

```go
func (c *Controller) sanitizeLookupRepoInput(in *LookupRepoInput) error {
    if in.RepoType == "" && in.URL == "" {
        return ErrRepoMissing
    }
    parsedURL, err := url.Parse(in.URL)
    if err != nil {
        return ErrInvalidURL
    }
    if parsedURL.Scheme == "" {
        return ErrBadURLScheme
    }
    // NO private IP check
    return nil
}
```

`detectDefaultGitBranch` (scm.go lines 113-130) then runs:

```go
cmd := command.New("ls-remote",
    command.WithFlag("--symref"),
    command.WithFlag("-q"),
    command.WithArg(gitRepoDir),  // attacker URL
    command.WithArg("HEAD"),
)
```

`git ls-remote` makes an actual TCP connection and HTTP GET to `<url>/info/refs?service=git-upload-pack`. The resulting error distinguishes open from closed ports (see PoC below), providing a port-scanning oracle.

Contrast with the webhook service (app/services/webhook/http_client.go), which explicitly blocks private IPs via a post-DNS DialContext check -- that guard is entirely absent in the gitspace SCM code path.

### PoC
(available upon request)

### Impact

An authenticated attacker with InfraProviderView access can:

1. Enumerate open TCP ports on internal hosts (distinguishable error messages for open vs. closed ports).
2. Reach cloud instance metadata endpoints (`169.254.169.254`, `fd00:ec2::254`) to probe for credential exposure depending on metadata endpoint behavior.
3. Send HTTP requests with git-specific headers to any internal HTTP service reachable from the server.

In multi-tenant Harness installations, any project member can trigger the SSRF against the internal network hosting the Harness deployment (AWS VPC, GCP VPC, Kubernetes cluster internal CIDRs, etc.).

milestone.title: M3 - Execution Sandbox & Egress Control
milestone.description: Disposable sandboxes, hardened image, scoped egress gateway, session manager, browser, OOB, kill switch.

items.body:
## Summary
Build the gateway's DNS resolver (`miekg/dns`) that answers only for in-scope names, resolves each name once and pins the chosen IP for the life of the connection/request, and blocks answers that point at private/metadata/link-local ranges. This is the anti-DNS-rebinding control required by S8.2.

## Context
Per CONTEXT_PACK S5 the gateway uses `miekg/dns` for scoped DNS. S8.2 requires: redirects and DNS answers to out-of-scope destinations blocked; anti-rebinding = resolve once, pin IP, re-check; private/link-local/metadata blocked unless explicitly in scope. Used by the HTTP proxy (EGRESS-005/006) and SOCKS5 (EGRESS-007).

## Scope
**In scope:** a resolver component with a per-request/connection pin cache; upstream resolution via a configured resolver; range blocking; optional DNS listener for tools that do their own lookups.
**Out of scope:** the scope matcher internals (EGRESS-004), private-range list definition shared with EGRESS-009.

## Detailed requirements
1. `internal/dnsresolve.Resolver.Resolve(ctx, host, pinKey) (net.IP, error)`: resolve `host` once via the upstream resolver (`GATEWAY_DNS_UPSTREAM`, default system), choose a single A/AAAA, and store `pinKey -> IP` in a short-TTL cache (`GATEWAY_DNS_PIN_TTL` default `120s`). Subsequent lookups for the same `pinKey+host` return the pinned IP.
2. Reject resolution for a name not in scope (host-level check via EGRESS-004) with `ErrHostOutOfScope`.
3. After resolution, check the IP against the blocked ranges (private, link-local, loopback, CGNAT, multicast, metadata `169.254.169.254` and `fd00:ec2::254`) unless that exact IP/CIDR is explicitly in the envelope scope -> else `ErrBlockedRange` (coordinate the list with EGRESS-009).
4. Optional DNS listener on `GATEWAY_DNS_ADDR` that only answers in-scope names with the pinned IP and returns `REFUSED`/`NXDOMAIN` otherwise; it never recurses for out-of-scope names.
5. CNAME chains: follow server-side but validate the **final** resolved IP; also validate that each intermediate name stays in scope if the policy requires it (`GATEWAY_DNS_STRICT_CNAME` default true).
6. Expose the pinned IP so the connecting component dials exactly it (no second resolution).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] In-scope name resolves and is pinned; a second resolution within TTL returns the same IP.
- [ ] Out-of-scope name -> `ErrHostOutOfScope`, no upstream query leaked for disallowed names via the listener.
- [ ] Name resolving to a private/metadata IP -> `ErrBlockedRange`.
- [ ] Rebinding simulation (upstream returns a public IP then a private IP) -> connection still uses the first pinned public IP.
- [ ] IPv6 and IPv4 both covered.

## Edge cases & failure modes
- Multiple A records -> pick deterministically (first after sort) and pin; do not round-robin mid-connection.
- TTL 0 / very low upstream TTL -> still honour the pin for the pin window.
- DNS timeout/SERVFAIL -> `ErrResolveFailed`, fail closed.
- Wildcard/dangling CNAME to out-of-scope -> blocked.
- IDN names -> IDNA normalise before scope check.
- Cache poisoning attempt via crafted answers -> only the chosen record is used; range + scope re-checked.
- Metadata endpoint via DNS name -> blocked by range check.

## Security, privacy & audit
Core anti-rebinding control (S8.2), deterministic (S8.11). Audit `egress.dns_blocked{reason}` with host + (hashed) resolved IP. No PII. The pin cache is keyed by run/connection so no cross-run leakage (S8.6).

## Observability
Metrics `egress_dns_queries_total{result}`, `egress_dns_blocked_total{reason}`, `egress_dns_pin_hits_total`. Logs `component=dns` with `host`, `pinned_ip`, `result`. Span `dns.resolve`.

## Test plan
- Unit: pinning, range blocking, CNAME final-IP validation.

🚨 **Severity:** HIGH
💡 **Vulnerability:** Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). The application acts as an AI Gateway and allowed users to supply custom `baseUrl` endpoints for LLM providers (e.g. OpenAI compatible, Ollama). These URLs were passed directly to `fetch()` without validation. An attacker could exploit this to scan internal networks or exfiltrate sensitive cloud credentials by querying metadata services (e.g. `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data`).
🎯 **Impact:** Potential unauthorized access to internal network resources, cloud instance metadata, and sensitive environment variables/credentials.
🔧 **Fix:** 
1. Created `server/security.ts` with a `validateSafeUrl` function. This function validates the protocol (only allowing `http`/`https`), allows local development loopback addresses, and critically, performs a DNS resolution to block the resolved IP if it points to known AWS metadata endpoints (`169.254.169.254`, `fd00:ec2::254`). 
2. Integrated `validateSafeUrl` into `server/orchestrator.ts`, `server/modelsFetcher.ts`, and `server.ts` wherever user-supplied URLs are fetched. 
3. Explicitly set `redirect: "error"` in all outbound AI fetch calls. This prevents attackers from bypassing the initial IP validation by supplying a benign URL that responds with a HTTP 302 redirect pointing back to an internal metadata IP. 

*(Note: While the DNS lookup validates the URL initially, native Node.js `fetch` is still theoretically susceptible to TOCTOU DNS rebinding since it performs its own subsequent resolution. Full mitigation requires using a custom Undici agent, but this fix drastically reduces the attack surface while preserving TLS SNI).*
✅ **Verification:** Verified by attempting to fetch the metadata endpoint locally, which was successfully blocked with `Access to internal metadata endpoints is blocked for security.` Added journal entry.

items.title: T19: Credential proxy egress allowlist
items.body:
Implements [T19](https://github.com/agentsky/agent-core/blob/main/docs/tasks-plan.md#t19). Stacked on #22; it will be re-chained later.

## Changes

- `cred_proxy::EgressProxy`, served on the proxy listener through `CredProxy::with_egress`. Without it, `CONNECT` still gets T18's 405. For each `CONNECT` it:
  - finds the session from the peer address in the `Registry`. An unknown address gets 403.
  - takes the target from the request line only. The target must be authority-form `host:port` over HTTP/1, with no user info. `Host` is ignored. HTTP/2 `CONNECT` is refused.
  - lowercases the host and drops one trailing dot. The host must be a DNS name with at least two labels, and the last label must start with a letter. That refuses IP literals and forms like `127.1`, `2130706433` and `0x7f.1`.
  - always refuses `api.anthropic.com`.
  - takes a tunnel place (see Limits), then checks the host against `[proxy] allow` rules first, then against the session's `EgressExtension` rules (the extension point for T25). Rules are exact hosts or `*.suffix`, on port 443 unless a rule names another port. A host that a rule names on a different port gets its own reason.
  - resolves the host once, as an FQDN so search domains don't apply. If any address in the answer is unreachable, the host is refused.
  - connects to the addresses it checked, never to the name. It answers 200 and copies bytes both ways with no TLS interception.
- Addresses that are never reachable, whichever rule allowed the host:
  - agentd's listener addresses and the sandbox subnet
  - private ranges: `10/8`, `172.16/12`, `192.168/16`, `fc00::/7`
  - loopback and link-local, including `169.254.169.254`
  - cloud metadata and platform addresses: AWS `fd00:ec2::254`, GCP `fd20:ce::254`, Oracle `fd00:c1::a9fe:a9fe`, Azure WireServer `168.63.129.16`, Alibaba `100.100.100.200` (in `100.64/10`), Oracle `192.0.0.192` (in `192.0.0/24`)
  - `0/8`, `100.64/10`, `192.0.0/24`
  - documentation, benchmarking, multicast, reserved and broadcast ranges
  - IPv6 outside `2000::/3`, plus `2001::/23`, `2002::/16`, `2001:db8::/32` and `3fff::/20`. This blocks NAT64, 6to4, Teredo and IPv4-compatible addresses that embed IPv4.
- Limits (`cred_proxy::EgressLimits`, `EgressProxy::with_limits`):
  - tunnel places, taken before the extension is asked or the host is looked up, and given back when the `CONNECT` is refused or the tunnel closes: 32 per session (429 past it) and 256 in all (503). agentd's `[proxy] max_session_tunnels` and `max_tunnels` set them.
  - at most 32 host lookups at once. Each lookup runs in its own task and keeps its place until `getaddrinfo` returns, even after the 5 s timeout has refused its `CONNECT`, because the timeout can't cancel a blocking lookup. A `CONNECT` that can't get a place within the timeout gets 503.
  - the `EgressExtension` gets 2 s to answer. After that the `CONNECT` gets 503.
  - a tunnel ends when either side closes, after 5 idle minutes, after 1 hour in any case, when its session has no live placeholder left, or when the proxy is dropped.
- Revoking cuts tunnels. The proxy watches each tunnel's session through the shared `Registry`. When a session's last placeholder goes (`revoke`, `revoke_session`, or a mint for another session at the same address), the registry drops the watch sender. So T23's `revoke_session` in `process_stopping` closes the session's tunnels with no other call. The T23 plan text says so.
- A refusal is 403, or 429/503 at a limit, or 502 when resolving or connecting fails. The body is one line of fixed plain text. Every refusal is logged with the session. A host is logged only after it has been checked, and the request line never is.
- `EGRESS_ENV` holds `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY` and `NO_PROXY` in both upper and lower case, ready for T23.
- agentd config: a new optional `[proxy]` section with `allow`, `max_tunnels` and `max_session_tunnels`, validated at load time. Errors name the entry, e.g. `proxy.allow.1`. `api.anthropic.com` is refused as a rule. `Config::egress_proxy()` is added for T23. The example config and README document the section.
- `Cidr` moves unchanged from agentd to `core_types::net`, with its tests, so cred-proxy can use it.
- Plan updated: T19 limits and acceptance, the T23 wiring, and a Deferred work entry. impl-notes `## T19` section updated.

## Choices the plan left open

- Egress is allowed whenever the source address has a live placeholder, not only while a turn runs.
- If an answer mixes allowed and denied addresses, the whole host is refused.
- All connection attempts to one host share a single 10 s deadline.
- `Network` is a trait so tests can fake resolution and connections.
- The extension is only asked when no configured rule allows the host.
- `*.suffix` matches any depth below the suffix, but not the suffix itself.
- `api.anthropic.com` is refused as a rule, in config and from the extension alike. A wildcard above it, like `*.anthropic.com`, is accepted and still never reaches it.
- Tunnels are closed through the `Registry` rather than an `EgressProxy::close_session`, because `CredProxy` owns the proxy and T23 would otherwise need its own handle to it.
- The PR is about 3,000 changed lines. Most of it is tests and the moved `Cidr` code, so I didn't split it.

## Deviations from the plan

- `Cidr` now lives in core-types instead of agentd.
- Private ranges are always denied, as the plan says. An earlier revision had an `[proxy] allow_private` key. Review showed it applied to every rule, including extension rules and wildcards, on any port, so it has been removed. Per-rule private access (a configured host plus its subnets, never for extension rules or wildcards) is recorded under the plan's Deferred work.

## Not verified live

- The native Claude Code build honoring `NO_PROXY`. I checked the npm build of 2.1.285 against two local capture servers:
  - with `NO_PROXY` naming the base URL's host, `/v1/messages` went directly to the base URL.
  - without it, the request went to `HTTP_PROXY` in absolute form, which the proxy refuses.
  - T23's live check should confirm this on the native build.
- agentd serving the proxy router: that wiring is T23.

## Verified

- Locally, on the affected crates:
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo test --locked --all-features -p cred-proxy -p agentd -p core-types`. The egress suite ran 5 times in a row with no flakes.
  - `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --all-features -p cred-proxy -p agentd`
- New tests:
  - an extension rule resolving to a private address (`evil-skill.example.net:22` → `10.20.9.9`) is refused
  - each new metadata address is denied
  - an `api.anthropic.com` rule is refused in config
  - the per-session and global tunnel caps; refused `CONNECT`s give their place back
  - lookups the timeout gave up on still count toward the lookup cap
  - an extension that never answers gets 503
  - a busy tunnel closes at its lifetime
  - revoking a session, or minting over its address, closes its tunnels and leaves other sessions' tunnels open
  - a registry unit test for the session watch
- CI's Docker tests job ran `docker_a_sandbox_clones_from_an_allowed_host_only` on the first revision, and it passed:
  - the github.com clone works through the proxy
  - the gitlab.com clone gets `403 from proxy after CONNECT`
  - a clone without the proxy fails
- An earlier local run needed the intercepting proxy's CA mounted into the container. CI needs no CA.

items.title: eks-security + eks-build: admission-webhook HA + Pod Identity link-local egress gaps

labels.name: deep-dive-feedback
labels.description: 2026-09 skills evaluation batch: external evaluation and the maintainer sweep it prompted

items.body:
## Summary

eks-security carries no admission-webhook failure-mode or HA guidance, so a Kyverno/OPA webhook set to `failurePolicy: Fail` with no HA (a single replica) blocks all scheduling when its pod is down, and it has no carve-out for the EKS Pod Identity link-local endpoint under default-deny egress, which gets misdiagnosed as an IAM error. Separately, eks-build's pod-scoped `NO_PROXY`/`no_proxy` list omits the Pod Identity endpoints (`169.254.170.23` and its IPv6 form) and its `:73` label mis-names the ECS task-role address. The ask adds webhook HA (3 replicas + PDB + system-namespace exemption), the egress carve-out and `NO_PROXY` entries, and a credential-caching troubleshooting note.

## Evidence

**Gap, not conflict:** eks-security has zero `failurePolicy` / fail-open / fail-closed text in either copy; the topic is covered elsewhere — `eks-best-practices/references/reliability-core.md:76` (`failurePolicy: Ignore` under "Admission Webhook Safety") and `references/observability.md:491`, eks-build's two-phase rule (`SKILL.md:134`, `references/pattern-guide.md:53`, `references/lessons-learned.md:60`), eks-recon's verbatim `failurePolicy` reporting (`references/security.md:552-648`, devops `:518-599`) and the ingress-migration nginx-admission caution — but none of it is the Kyverno/OPA self-DoS + HA guidance a hardening reader needs. A Kyverno webhook with `failurePolicy: Fail` and no HA blocks all scheduling when its pod is down; require 3 replicas + PDB + system-namespace exemption. Second gap: default-deny egress blocks the EKS Pod Identity link-local endpoint `169.254.170.23` (`AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI=http://169.254.170.23/v1/credentials` per the "How EKS Pod Identity Agent works with a Pod" section of the EKS "Understand how EKS Pod Identity works" page) — 0 hits in eks-security; misdiagnosed as IAM at runtime. Third (found during maintainer review), eks-build's `NO_PROXY` lists carry `169.254.170.2` (the ECS task-role endpoint, irrelevant on EKS nodes) at `customization-guide.md:56` (node `/etc/profile.d`), `:68` (containerd) and `:82` (pod env), and `:73` mislabels it "credential provider"; the operative gap is the pod-scoped list (`:82`) and the `:73` label, since Pod Identity resolves credentials from `169.254.170.23` inside the pod — node and containerd auth go through IMDS / the node role and never touch the `.23` endpoint, so adding it to those node/containerd lists is harmless, not required. The EKS "Learn how EKS Pod Identity grants pods access" page (Considerations) says to add `169.254.170.23` (IPv4) and `[fd00:ec2::23]` (IPv6) to `no_proxy`/`NO_PROXY`, and both are absent from the pod-scoped list.

## Proposed scope

Add a troubleshooting note on credential caching: IAM **permission-policy** edits need no pod restart — AWS evaluates the applicable policies against each request's context (IAM User Guide, "Policy evaluation logic"), subject to IAM eventual consistency (a change "might not be visible until the previously cached data times out", IAM User Guide, "Changes that I make are not always immediately visible"); changing the **association** (role ARN, target role, session policy) "does not reset the existing cache" — currently 6 hours, or 59 minutes when a target role is set, per the "Caching considerations" section of the EKS "Access AWS resources using EKS Pod Identity target IAM roles" page — so recreate the workload pods or wait for expiry.

## Impact

Hardening readers can lock a cluster out of scheduling, or spend time misdiagnosing blocked Pod Identity credentials as IAM failures; the EKS-security items were raised by roughly 6 reviewers and the eks-build NO_PROXY item was found during maintainer review.

- #170

items.title: [FEAT] ECS: vend task-role credentials to security-group protected tasks
items.body:
## Service

ECS

## API Action / Feature

Task IAM roles: vend credentials to task containers that run under security-group enforcement.

## AWS Documentation

- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/task-iam-roles.html
- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdkref/latest/guide/feature-container-credentials.html

## Why is this needed?

#4486 wired up task-role credentials, with one case deliberately left out: a task running under security-group enforcement gets none. Its containers attach with `--network container:<helperId>` and share the firewall helper's network namespace rather than joining the ECS Docker network, so the per-network proxy holding `169.254.170.2` is not reachable from them. `EcsContainerManager` logs a warning and starts the task without `AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_RELATIVE_URI`.

The reason it is worth closing rather than leaving documented: the task still starts, and it keeps Floci's baseline credentials. Its effective identity is the default account rather than the role it asked for, so an IAM policy test against that task passes whether or not the role would have allowed the call. Turning on security-group enforcement silently changes what a task can do.

## Options

Three ways I can see, and I do not think the choice is obvious.

**A. Give the firewall helper a link-local address.** Every protected container already shares that namespace, so one address on the helper covers the whole task, which actually fits the shared-namespace model better than the per-container allocation used on the normal path. Needs the helper to join the ECS network alongside its ENI, and needs an nftables exception for `169.254.170.2:80`. Smallest change to the credential path, but it puts a hole in the namespace whose whole purpose is not to have one, and the exception has to be narrow enough that a workload cannot ride it somewhere else.

**B. Run the proxy inside the protected namespace.** Instead of reaching out to the shared network, the helper itself holds `169.254.170.2` on its loopback or a dummy interface and forwards to Floci. Keeps the protected namespace closed and needs no change to the shared network. Costs a second proxy mechanism to maintain next to `EcsCredentialsProxy`, and puts another process in the helper.

**C. Use `AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI` over loopback.** For protected tasks only, publish `AWS_CONTAINER_CREDENTIALS_FULL_URI=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v2/credentials/<id>` and have the helper listen on loopback inside the shared namespace. No link-local address, no `169.254.170.2`, and no exception in the nftables table, since the traffic never leaves the namespace.

On C, the SDK support is better than I expected. The container credential provider page lists every SDK as supporting `FULL_URI`, and AWS's own example is `http://localhost:8080/get-credentials`, so this is not a niche path. botocore's validator (`ContainerMetadataFetcher._validate_allowed_url`) accepts any loopback address over plain HTTP, alongside the `169.254.170.2` / `169.254.170.23` / `fd00:ec2::23` / `localhost` allowlist. It is also the one option where real ECS and Floci would differ in what the container sees, which may or may not matter for your purposes.

I lean C, mainly because it is the only one that does not weaken the isolation the feature exists to provide, but B is the more faithful emulation and A is the least code. Happy to be talked out of it.

@hectorvent when you have a moment, could you weigh in on which direction you want before I start? The nftables and namespace side is your design, and I would rather not pick for you.

## Are you willing to contribute a PR?

- [x] Yes
- [ ] No

items.body:
## 背景 (Why)

租戶的 editor 在雲端設定設備的主機與連接埠（設備 API，Laysi/trustiot-v2#100，PR Laysi/trustiot-v2#624），閘道器的 agent 依設定以 Modbus 輪詢。設備 API 拒絕字面上指向閘道器本身的主機：loopback 位址（含 `::ffff:127.0.0.1`）、`localhost`、`*.localhost`、`ip6-localhost`、`ip6-loopback`，以及解析器會讀成數字的名稱（例如 `0x7f000001`）。

但雲端無法照閘道器在現場網路上的方式解析名稱。任何 DNS 名稱都可能在現場解析成 loopback，或在 API 檢查之後才改成 loopback（DNS rebinding）。這時 agent 會把 Modbus 請求送到閘道器本機的連接埠，輪詢的設定就成了探測閘道器本機服務的管道，讀到的回應還會變成遙測回到雲端。

API 的檢查只是輸入檢查，不是安全邊界（`services/assets/README.md` 的「設備」）。真正的把關必須在閘道器解析與連線的那一刻。這是 2026-10-24 Laysi/trustiot-v2#100 提交前的審查關卡與安全審查指出的問題。

**這是 Laysi/trustiot-v2#93 的前置條件，不是延後的進階驗證。** Laysi/trustiot-v2#93（gateway-ops）一開始把設備設定下發到閘道器，租戶寫的主機就會被閘道器實際連線。所以這個防護必須在 #93 下發設定之前完成，不能降為 P2（組織規範「安全關卡的階段性要求」）。

## 範圍 (What)

### 包含

- `edge/agent/src/modbus/tcp.rs` 的 `connect`（目前是 `TcpStream::connect((host, port))`，解析與連線一起做）：
  - 先把主機解析成 `SocketAddr` 清單（例如 `tokio::net::lookup_host`），檢查每個位址，再直接連到檢查過的 `SocketAddr`。不能把名稱再交給連線函式，否則會解析第二次，DNS rebinding 就能繞過檢查。
  - 比對前先把 IPv4-mapped 的 IPv6 位址轉回 IPv4（`IpAddr::to_canonical`）。
  - 拒絕下列位址：
    - loopback（127.0.0.0/8、`::1`）
    - 未指定（`0.0.0.0`、`::`）
    - 閘道器自己網卡上的位址（連線時讀目前的介面位址，因為 DHCP 可能改變它）
    - 多播（224.0.0.0/4、`ff00::/8`）
    - 廣播（`255.255.255.255`，以及閘道器各介面網段的廣播位址）
    - 雲端 metadata 位址：`169.254.169.254` 與 `fd00:ec2::254`
  - 169.254.0.0/16 的其他位址照常允許：沒有 DHCP 的 RS485 轉換器常用 APIPA 位址。私有位址（10/8、172.16/12、192.168/16、IPv6 ULA）也照常允許，現場設備就在這些網段。
  - 所有位址都被拒絕時回 `ReadError::Connect`，訊息寫明「位址指向閘道器本身或不允許的位址」，不帶解析結果以外的資料。
  - IP 位址的寫法也走同一條檢查：設定若經別的路徑下發，閘道器仍要擋。
- 測試的開關：edge 的測試都把 agent 指向 127.0.0.1 上的假 Modbus 端點（`crates/testkit` 的 `FakeModbus`），所以這個限制要能在測試裡關掉，例如 `TcpConnection` 的一個建構參數，或只在 `#[cfg(test)]` 或測試 feature 才存在的設定。正式的設定路徑（設定檔、環境變數、MQTT 下發的設定）不能打開它。

  - 169.254.1.20 這類 APIPA 位址可以連。

AWS has recently added an IPv6 endpoint for IMDS, in addition to the existing 169.254.169.254 IPv4 endpoint. On EC2 instances with IPv6 addresses assigned, the metadata service is available at fd00:ec2::254

items.title: Default ruleset has no coverage for the WebFetch tool  IMDS and IOC-domain access bypass detection entirely
items.body:
What would you like to be added:
Two macros and corresponding rules covering the WebFetch tool in rules/default/coding_agents_rules.yaml, mirroring the existing Bash-side patterns:

A macro/rule denying WebFetch calls targeting cloud instance metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254 and its known encoding variants, metadata.google.internal, metadata.azure.com), reusing the same IP-encoding list already hardened in the existing is_imds_access macro.
A macro/rule denying (or asking — see question below) WebFetch calls targeting a known malicious IOC hosting domain, reusing the contains_ioc_domain macro already defined for the MCP/skill-content checks.

- macro: is_webfetch_imds
  condition: >
    tool.name = "WebFetch"
    and (tool.input contains "169.254.169.254"
         or tool.input contains "metadata.google.internal"
         or tool.input contains "metadata.azure.com"
         or tool.input contains "fd00:ec2::254"
         or tool.input contains "2852039166"
         or tool.input contains "0xa9fea9fe"
         or tool.input contains "0Xa9fea9fe"
         or tool.input contains "0251.0376.0251.0376")
I can also add a WebSearch equivalent if that's in scope, and to write the actual PR once the shape is agreed.

Why is this needed:
The plugin already fully supports the WebFetch tool — it's parsed correctly and premptictl logs has dedicated pretty-printing for its url field, and the E2E test harness generates WebFetch events — but no rule in the default ruleset references tool.name = "WebFetch". That means:

An agent calling WebFetch directly against a cloud metadata endpoint to steal IAM credentials produces zero alerts, even though the identical attack via curl/wget through Bash is already denied by is_imds_access.
An agent fetching a known-malicious hosting domain (the same domains already enumerated in contains_ioc_domain for MCP/skill poisoning) via WebFetch also passes silently.
Even the informational "Monitor activity outside working directory" rule is scoped to Write/Edit/Read, so WebFetch gets no audit-trail coverage at all today.

Two questions before I put together a PR:

Does this fit best as additions to the existing "Threats" section, or would you rather see a dedicated network-access section given WebFetch/WebSearch are a distinct tool category from Bash?
Deny or ask for the IOC-domain case? Current precedent in the ruleset is mixed — MCP-install-from-IOC-domain is a deny, but MCP-config-referencing-base64 is an ask "because it's not conclusive." A WebFetch to a confirmed-bad domain feels closer to the deny case to me, but wanted your read before assuming.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefer the Bug issue type)

items.body:
**File:** plugin-api/src/main/java/com/infenia/yukta/plugin/util/HostAllowList.java (isMetadataAddress / inetAton, ~L124-155)

NUMERIC_HOST accepts `::ffff:169.254.169.254`, but inetAton splits on '.' and the first part `::ffff:169` fails to parse, so the address is judged not link-local. IPv4-mapped IPv6 (and e.g. fd00:ec2::254, the AWS IPv6 IMDS) pass the always-on metadata guard; with an empty allow-list the call goes through. Also, a URL that URI.create rejects yields host==null and, with an empty list, is allowed without the metadata check.

**Fix:** unwrap `::ffff:a.b.c.d` (and compat forms) to the IPv4 part before the check; add fd00:ec2::254; treat unparsable URLs as refused for the metadata check.

items.title: fix(wash-runtime): check the address wasi:http egress resolves to
items.body:
# fix(wash-runtime): check the address wasi:http egress resolves to

Branch: `fix/http-egress-address-check` (2 commits, stacked on `fix/hostpath-volume-gate`; the two are independent, the stack only gives the plugin-tls PRs a single base)

## Why

`EgressAddressPolicy` gated WASI sockets and native plugins but never the guest's `wasi:http` path. HTTP egress was checked by name (`allowedHosts`), and nothing checked where that name resolved. A guest allowed `*`, or any name it controls, could point that name at:

- `127.0.0.1` / `::1`: the host's ingress, control-plane ports, or another tenant's published port.
- `169.254.169.254`, `[fd00:ec2::254]`, or `::ffff:169.254.169.254`: the cloud metadata service.

HTTP is the path most workloads use, so the weaker check sat on the more common path.

**Why P0:** the host-wide client identity that shipped in `client_identity.rs` has no per-destination scoping. With it configured, the host also presents its client certificate to whatever answers. That turns this from SSRF into credential disclosure to an endpoint the guest chooses. (Workload Identity RFC, carried forward from `c89eb489e`.)

## What

There was no point in the HTTP stack where the resolved address was visible. Both call paths now have one:

- **Pooled `wasi:http` and pooled gRPC (`BoundedConnector`).** Each new connection builds an `HttpConnector` whose resolver (`GatedResolver`) passes every resolved address through the host's `EgressAddressGate` and hands the connector only what it permits.
  - The address checked is the address dialed; nothing is resolved twice.
  - The URI keeps the hostname, so SNI and `Host` are unchanged.
  - The resolver is built per connect because hyper-util does not tell a resolver the port, and the host-owned-port check needs it.
  - hyper-util never resolves an address literal, so the connector judges a literal itself, before it takes a quota permit.
- **Unpooled gRPC fallback (`send_grpc_request` → `connect_http_tcp`).** It resolves once, filters, and dials the filtered list.
- **One source of truth.** `EgressAddressGate::from_socket_policy` reads `egress_addrs`, `egress_mode`, `host_owned_ports` and `meters` from the host's `SocketPolicy`, and the range check is `EgressAddressPolicy::permits`, unchanged.
  - `HostBuilder::build` installs the gate through new `HostHandler::install_egress_gate` / `OutgoingHandler::install_egress_gate` hooks. An embedder that configured only the engine (Control included) therefore gets HTTP gated exactly like sockets, with no new wiring.
  - Both hooks default to no-ops, so a custom transport keeps its own behavior.
- **Host-owned ports.** Once the range policy has passed an address, a loopback or unspecified spelling is judged as the loopback address the host's reservations are keyed on, and an exact direct-bind address is judged as itself.
- **Error surface.** A request with no permitted address fails with `DestinationIpProhibited`, not `ConnectionRefused`, and the `DenyReason` is logged.

## Semantics

- `--socket-egress=count` (the default) severs nothing. Each refusal increments `would_deny` and logs at `debug`. The flag's help and the chart doc now say it covers `wasi:http` addresses too.
- `enforce` drops refused candidates, so mixed resolution connects to the permitted address and fails only when none survive.
- Reused pooled connections are not checked again: they were checked when made (`http_client.rs` connector doc).
- Component plugins' `wasi:http` goes through the same handler and is gated the same way.

## Also in this PR (Issue 5)

A docs commit states in the `wash` config schema and the chart's plugin `allowedHosts` entry that a native plugin gets endpoint-declaration checks, not resolved-address checks, and recommends literal IP addresses where the stronger guarantee matters. The issue suggested "IP/CIDR", but `AllowedHost` has no CIDR form, so the docs say literal IP addresses only.

## Out of scope (per the issue)

- Flipping `EgressMode` to `Enforce`.
- Native-plugin resolved-address filtering, which can't be intercepted by construction.

## Tests

- `host::egress_policy`: keeps the permitted candidates and drops the rest in order (mixed resolution), refuses when nothing survives (loopback, `::1`, metadata v4/v6/mapped), count mode keeps everything and counts, host-owned ports refused through every loopback spelling and a direct bind.
- `host::http_client`:
  - `localhost` (the DNS path) and a literal loopback are refused under enforce, with zero connections reaching the server.
  - The metadata address is refused in every spelling.
  - Count mode connects and counts.
  - Pooled gRPC is gated.
  - The unpooled connect dials only what the gate permits.
  - TLS to a permitted host arrives with SNI `localhost` and a certificate verified for that name.
- `host::tests::the_host_gates_http_egress_with_its_socket_policy`: a `Host` built from an enforcing engine gates the pooled path, pooled gRPC, and the unpooled gRPC fallback, with no other wiring.
- `cargo test -p wash-runtime --lib` (987 passed). Integration: `integration_http_{allowed_hosts,egress_pooling,tls,local_routing,call_timeout,ip_name_lookup}`, and `integration_plugin_http_egress` with `host-component-plugins`. Clippy with all targets.

## Notes for review

- An `OutgoingHandler` that makes its own connections should call `EgressAddressGate::filter` on what it resolves. The hook's doc says so, but nothing forces it.
- The gate treats the machine's routable addresses (the pod IP) as ordinary destinations, as the socket path does. Reaching the host's ingress through its pod IP is the same as reaching it from any other pod.

## 背景 (Why)

舊系統的防火牆擋住現場設備（Laysi/trustiot#140）：轉換器的 port 各不相同（實測過 502、8886），不能用固定白名單；另有註冊 fail-open（Laysi/trustiot#119）與 PIN 外洩（Laysi/trustiot#121）。資料分割區加密後，整台被偷仍會開機自動解鎖，D5（閘道器映像與強化）靠登入面強化讓人登不進去；改開機分割區取得 root 這條路則要等 MS6 的 secure boot。

## 範圍 (What)

### 包含

- 依設定中的設備清單動態開放 fieldbus 出口（主機與 port），移除設備時關閉
- 對雲端只需要 443 出口
- 閘道器開機時確認已完成出廠登錄並持有有效憑證，否則不進入運作狀態（舊系統的註冊 fail-open，Laysi/trustiot#119）；TPM 金鑰的 PIN（若用 tpm2-pkcs11）不經命令列與環境變數（Laysi/trustiot#121）
- SSH 只收金鑰；螢幕與 USB 關閉；serial 緊急密碼每台隨機
- 防火牆規則由獨立的特權元件依已套用的設定更新（只接受主機與 port 清單），agent 維持非 root；機制在本 issue 決定
- nftables 的 output chain：對 agent 的 uid 拒絕 `fib daddr type { local, broadcast, multicast }`、`169.254.169.254` 與 `fd00:ec2::254`。這是 agent 位址防護（只看 `getifaddrs`）底下的核心層，也涵蓋 hairpin NAT、回到閘道器本機的 port forward 與 `ip route add local`（2026-10-24 自 Laysi/trustiot-v2#653 的安全審查加入）。其他雲端的 metadata 位址（例如 `100.100.100.200`、`168.63.129.16`、`169.254.170.2`）只有 VM 形態的閘道器才需要。
- 不變量：閘道器上的本機服務只聽 loopback 或 unix socket，不聽其他介面（同上，Laysi/trustiot-v2#653）。

### 不包含

- 遠端維護通道（Laysi/trustiot-v2#186）

## 現狀 (State)

尚未開始（2026-10-10 建立）。前置 issue 完成後才能開始，清單見「指標」與 GitHub 的 blocked by 關係。

2026-10-24 自 Laysi/trustiot-v2#653 的安全審查（Low 2、Info 7）加入：agent uid 的 nftables output chain 與本機服務只聽 loopback 或 unix socket 的不變量，見「範圍」與「驗收條件」。

## 驗收條件 (Acceptance Criteria)

- [ ] 新增設備後該主機與 port 可連、其他被擋；移除後關閉（測試）
- [ ] SSH 密碼登入被拒（檢查）

Adds cloud-metadata addresses to `ALWAYS_BLOCKED_METADATA_IPS`. They stay blocked under every flag combination, including `allow_private_ips=True`:

- `168.63.129.16`: Azure WireServer. It is public address space, so no private-range check caught it.
- `fd20:ce::254`: GCP metadata server over IPv6. It is a ULA, so `allow_private_ips=True` used to permit it.
- `fd00:ec2::23`: AWS EKS Pod Identity credentials over IPv6. It is a ULA, as above.
- `169.254.42.42` and `fd00:42::42`: Scaleway instance metadata.
- `fd00:a9fe:a9fe::1`: Akamai / Linode metadata over IPv6.
- `fd00:c1::a9fe:a9fe`: Oracle Cloud (OCI) IMDS over IPv6.
- `fe80::a9fe:a9fe`: OpenStack Nova and Hetzner metadata over IPv6.

Every consumer of the shared set picks these up: the SSRF validator, the egress policy, content and result fetching, notifications, and the LLM and embedding provider URL guard. Mapped, NAT64-wrapped and `%zone` spellings are covered. The label on `169.254.170.23` is corrected to EKS Pod Identity.

No behaviour change for local or private endpoints. In particular, the provider URL guard (`assert_base_url_safe`) still accepts link-local destinations, because rootless Podman 5.3+ maps `host.containers.internal` and `host-gateway` to `169.254.1.2`. An earlier commit on this branch had made it refuse link-local; that was reverted here and will be proposed separately as a breaking change.

Validation: an earlier revision passed focused provider, validator and stored-setting tests. The latest commits (the link-local revert, the further metadata addresses, test adjustments and docs) have only been checked with py_compile, ruff and isolated validator drivers. CI is pending.

items.title: rest-api: pin the vetted IP at webhook connect (close SSRF TOCTOU DNS-rebind)
items.body:
## Summary

The webhook publisher's SSRF guard (`assert_safe_webhook_url`) resolves the target host and rejects blocked IP ranges **before** delivery, but `httpx` then re-resolves the hostname **independently** at connect time. The connection is not pinned to the vetted IP, so a low-TTL attacker-controlled DNS record can return a public IP to the guard's lookup and a private/metadata IP to httpx's connect — classic DNS rebinding (TOCTOU).

Deferred from the rest-api build (#61); flagged by the adversarial security review as MINOR.

## Why this is MINOR, not urgent (mitigations already in place)

- `httpx.AsyncClient` uses `follow_redirects=False`, so the redirect-to-metadata SSRF vector is already closed.
- The guard runs before **every** delivery attempt (small TOCTOU window).
- The blocklist is comprehensive: loopback, link-local + `169.254.169.254`, RFC1918, `0.0.0.0/8`, ULA + `fd00:ec2::254`, and IPv4-mapped forms — checked against **all** resolved A/AAAA records.
- `getaddrinfo` now runs via `run_in_threadpool`, off the serve event loop.

## Fix

Resolve once in the guard, then connect to the **vetted IP** while preserving the `Host` header (and SNI for HTTPS webhooks) — e.g. a custom httpx transport / SSRF-safe transport that validates the peer IP at connect time. Keep the pre-attempt guard as defense in depth.

## Location

`src/carve/api/webhooks.py` — `attempt_delivery` (carries an in-code `# NOTE(rest-api): see issue` marker).

## Scope / priority

Security MINOR. Schedule before hosted/multi-user, or before webhooks to arbitrary external URLs are broadly relied upon. Capability: [rest-api](../blob/main/specs/capabilities/rest-api.md).

items.title: [security] Webhook delivery is a server-side SSRF vector (no private/metadata IP block)
items.body:
## Summary

Tenants register webhook URLs; the control plane POSTs to them on deploy/activate events. Validation in `validateWebhookRequest` (`edge-control-plane/internal/handler/webhook.go:147`) only checks the URL is a valid `https` URL — there is **no block on private / link-local / metadata IP ranges**, and delivery uses a bare `&http.Client{Timeout: 10s}` with the default transport (`edge-control-plane/internal/service/webhook.go:114`): no restricting dialer, no DNS-rebind guard.

## Impact

Server-side request forgery from the control plane. A tenant can register:

- `https://10.0.0.5:8500/…` (internal service)
- `https://169.254.169.254/…` / `https://[fd00:ec2::254]/…` (cloud metadata)
- an attacker-controlled hostname that resolves to a public IP at registration and rebinds to an internal IP at delivery time

The CP then fires requests at internal targets. It is **semi-blind**: the per-attempt error/status is written to `webhook_deliveries`, which the tenant reads back — enough to port-scan and fingerprint the internal network via timing/error differences.

Reachable by any self-signup tenant.

## Note

The **guest** egress path already solves exactly this problem in `edge-runtime/src/egress.rs::is_blocked_ip` (loopback/private/link-local/ULA/IPv4-mapped/metadata + a DNS-rebind pre-resolve guard). The CP-side webhook path does not reuse any of it.

## Suggested remediation

- Resolve `wh.URL`'s host and reject if any candidate IP is in a blocked range (reuse the runtime's block-list logic).
- Install a custom `DialContext` that re-validates the connected IP (defeats DNS rebinding), mirroring `edge-runtime/src/egress_transport.rs`.
- Keep https-only.

Found in pre-release security audit (deeper pass).

items.title: feat(network): block requests to cloud metadata endpoints
items.body:
Cohere's report on an open-weight model ([link](https://cohere.com/blog/concerning-behaviour-popular-open-weight-ai-model)) shows the model reaching for the cloud metadata address before trying to upload data. Requests like `curl http://169.254.169.254/.../security-credentials/` were allowed at every level.

## What

- New `manual_only` rule `network.cloud-metadata` (category Network).
- It fires only when a request-capable command names a metadata host: HTTP/transfer clients (`curl`, `wget`, `aria2c`, `http(s)`, `xh(s)`, `httpie`, `fetch`, `lwp-request`), socket tools (`nc`, `ncat`, `netcat`, `socat`, `telnet`), or a code interpreter (`python -c`, `node -e`, …). Commands that only mention the address, such as `grep`, `git commit -m`, `iptables -d 169.254.169.254 -j DROP` or `sed`, are left alone.
- Hosts: `169.254.169.254`, `169.254.170.2`, `169.254.170.23`, `fd00:ec2::254`, `fd00:ec2::23`, `metadata.google.internal`, `metadata.goog`, `100.100.100.200` (Alibaba Cloud). Only whole-host matches count, so `169.254.169.2540` doesn't match.
- Wrappers are peeled first: `sudo`, `env`, `timeout`, `nohup`, `xargs`, `find -exec`. The request-client set joins the transparent-wrapper unwrapper so `timeout 10 curl …` is analyzed.

## Known gaps

This is a tool-call tripwire, not an egress sandbox. It doesn't catch:
- requests made from script files or dependencies;
- unlisted binaries (PowerShell `iwr`, `bun -e`, `deno eval`, `watch curl`);
- DNS aliases or numeric IP spellings;
- a heredoc body fed to `bash <<EOF` or `python3 <<PY`. That form was already unchecked by this rule before this PR, and `cat <<EOF | bash` is still blocked;
- a URL arriving on stdin (`printf url | xargs curl`);
- in `xargs`/`find`, any request-client word plus any metadata host anywhere in the argv blocks, without working out which command gets which argument.

## Validation

- Contract rows first: block rows for the report's command forms, allow rows for text-only mentions. Each failed before its fix.
- `bun run check`

items.title: Validate URLs and bound response sizes to block SSRF
items.body:
## What Changed

Closes #40.

The source-acquisition pipeline takes URLs returned by the web-search LLM in [`lib/pipeline/sources.ts:findSources`](lib/pipeline/sources.ts) and feeds them directly to `fetch` via [`lib/pipeline/pdf-validation.ts:rawFetch`](lib/pipeline/pdf-validation.ts). There is no scheme check, no host allow-list, no IP-range deny-list, and no body-size cap on `await res.arrayBuffer()`. A poisoned web-search result can drive the worker into requesting `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/...` (AWS IMDS), `http://[fd00:ec2::254]/...` (IPv6 IMDS), `http://localhost:5432/`, etc. — and an oversized response OOMs the worker. The same shape repeats in [`lib/integrations/reducto.ts`](lib/integrations/reducto.ts) at `downloadImage` (line ~266) and the presigned-result fetch in `fetchJobResult` (line ~212).

This PR adds defense in depth:

1. **New module `lib/safe-url.ts`** — single source of truth for URL safety:
   - `validateUrlShape(url, options)` — synchronous validator. Scheme allowlist (default `http:` / `https:`), IPv6 bracket-unwrap, IP-literal deny-list covering RFC 1918 (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16), 127/8 loopback, 169.254/16 link-local (AWS IMDS), 100.64/10 CGNAT, 0.0.0.0/8, IETF TEST-NET-1/2/3, multicast 224/4, reserved 240/4, broadcast, IPv6 `::1`, `fe80::/10`, `fc00::/7` ULA, `ff00::/8` multicast, IPv4-mapped `::ffff:…` re-checked against v4 rules. Plus a localhost-alias name list (`localhost`, `localhost.localdomain`, `ip6-localhost`, `ip6-loopback`, `metadata.google.internal`, `metadata`).
   - `validateUrlAsync(url, options)` — runs the shape validator, then `dns.lookup(host, { all: true })` and re-validates every A/AAAA record against the IP deny-list.
   - `boundedFetch(url, { maxBytes, timeoutMs, headers, redirect, allowedSchemes })` — fetch wrapper that runs `validateUrlAsync` before the request, streams the response body via `res.body.getReader()` and aborts past `maxBytes`, **re-validates the FINAL URL after redirects** (so a 302 from a public host to `169.254.169.254` is rejected even though the original URL passed).

2. **`lib/pipeline/pdf-validation.ts`** — `rawFetch` now delegates to `boundedFetch` with `maxBytes = 100 MiB` (well above any real vendor data-sheet). All four existing callers of `fetchAndValidatePdf` (`option-matrices.ts`, `sources.ts` × 2, `program-docs.ts`, `app/api/pipeline/sources/[id]/screenshot/route.ts`) inherit the validation transparently — no signature change.

3. **`lib/integrations/reducto.ts`** — `downloadImage` (LLM/Reducto-supplied image URLs) and `fetchJobResult` (presigned result follow) both route through `boundedFetch` with `maxBytes = 50 MiB`. The trusted Reducto API endpoints (`platform.reducto.ai/upload`, `/parse_async`, `/job/{id}`) are intentionally NOT routed through — they're trusted infrastructure with bearer auth, and going through the deny-list would just add latency.

## Scope Details

**No public API shape changes.** `rawFetch`, `fetchAndValidatePdf`, `downloadImage`, and `fetchJobResult` keep their existing signatures. Callers see exactly the same `{ ok, status, buf, contentType, error }` / `PdfValidationResult` / `DownloadImageResult` shapes — error paths now also surface a clear `"host X is a private/reserved IP"` / `"scheme X not allowed"` / `"body exceeded N bytes"` message instead of a generic network error.

**No dependency change, no schema change, no migration.** `node:dns/promises` and `node:net` are stdlib. Existing `npm run test` (4 files / 35 tests) passes unchanged.

**Known limitation — DNS rebinding.** Between `validateUrlAsync` and the actual `fetch`, a malicious DNS server can serve a different answer. True defense requires resolving once, then pinning the request to that IP via an undici Agent / dispatcher. Documented in the module header as a deliberate follow-up.

**Trusted endpoints kept out of the deny-list.** Calls to `platform.reducto.ai/{upload,parse_async,job}` in `reducto.ts:106/145/166` continue to use raw `fetch` — they're trusted infrastructure, bearer-authenticated, hardcoded host, no LLM input. Routing them through `boundedFetch` would add a DNS round-trip per call with no security benefit.

## Test Plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- [x] `npm run test` — 4 test files / 35 tests pass; no regressions.
- [x] Live deny-list repro against the new helpers — 13 attack URLs all rejected at the `validateUrlShape` step (no network IO):
  ```
  AWS IMDS v4         → "host 169.254.169.254 is a private/reserved IP"
  AWS IMDS v6         → "host fd00:ec2::254 is a private/reserved IP"
  loopback v4 / v6    → blocked
  localhost name      → "host localhost is a localhost alias"
  metadata.google.internal → blocked
  RFC 1918 10/8, 172.16, 192.168 → blocked
  ::ffff:127.0.0.1    → "host ::ffff:7f00:1 is a private/reserved IP"  (IPv4-mapped unwrap works)
  file://, gopher://, javascript: → "scheme X: not allowed"
  https://www.hpe.com/... (legitimate vendor PDF) → ok=true
  https://8.8.8.8/    (legitimate public IPv4)    → ok=true
  ```
- [x] `boundedFetch` against IMDS literal returns `{ ok: false, error: "host 169.254.169.254 is a private/reserved IP" }` without making any network request.
- [ ] Follow-up (out of scope for this PR): vitest coverage for each deny-list category + integration tests against a mock HTTP server for the `maxBytes` cap and redirect-to-private-IP rejection — sketched in the linked issue's "Tests" §4.
- [ ] Follow-up: DNS-rebinding hardening via an undici Agent that pins the request to the IP resolved at validation time.

items.title: Add --unsafe-network escape hatch + egress baseline deny-categories (ARD-0011, ARD-0036)

Two coupled egress gaps:

- **ARD-0011 `--unsafe-network` is absent.** `install-egress` only honors `enforce|learn`; the security model references an unsafe mode + a `security.unsafe_network_used` audit event that don't exist.
- **ARD-0036 egress baseline floor unbuilt.** `install-egress` still does a blanket `-A OUTPUT -d $NET_CIDR -j ACCEPT` with no top-of-chain `-I` baseline, so cloud-metadata (`169.254.169.254`) + link-local stay reachable — including under learn/unsafe modes. No `category:` on egress audit events.

Fix together: add the unconditional metadata/link-local floor (survives `--unsafe-network`), default-deny cross-sandbox/SMTP/SSH, wire `--unsafe-network` as a third mode, tag audit events. Touches `templates/_common/bin/install-egress`, `lib/egress.sh`, `boring`.
